If you dropped a penny from the top of the Empire State Building, could it kill someone?
Lots of people think it would hit like a bullet.
But a penny is flat and light, so the air pushes back hard against it.
After about fifty feet, it stops speeding up.
Then it flutters down like a leaf, at around twenty-five miles an hour.
A physicist tested this with wind tunnels and balloons, and pennies just bounced off his face.
So it would feel like a flick on the forehead.
A falling pen is different. Point down, it can drop like an arrow, fast enough to punch into wood.
